youtube.title: He Said the Price First and Still Won #Shorts
youtube.description:
Kai just broke the golden rule of haggling. And he's about to win.

In negotiation experiments, whichever side made the first offer tended to get the better outcome, and first offers strongly predicted the final price (Galinsky & Mussweiler, 2001). The first number works as an anchor: even a random wheel stopping on 10 or 65 moved people's guesses of Africa's share of UN members to 25% or 45% (Tversky & Kahneman, 1974). Going first works best when you know the real value; an extreme offer can make the other side walk away.

So, would you say the price first?

Sources:
- Galinsky & Mussweiler (2001), First offers as anchors, J. Personality and Social Psychology 81(4): https://www.kellogg.northwestern.edu/faculty/research/detail/2001/first-offers-as-anchors-the-role-of-perspective-taking
- Tversky & Kahneman (1974), Judgment under Uncertainty: Heuristics and Biases, Science 185: https://socialsci.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Psychology/Cognitive_Psychology/Cognitive_Psychology_(Andrade_and_Walker)/09%3A_Decision_Making/9.03%3A_Anchoring
- Harvard Program on Negotiation, When to make the first offer: https://www.pon.harvard.edu/daily/negotiation-skills-daily/when-to-make-the-first-offer-in-negotiations

Kai, Rosa and the flea market are fictional.
